notes: The 'Two manual and pedal base-line Phoenix Organ': 28 speaking stops, illuminated stop keys above the top manual. Most Phoenix organs are bespoke; this template only fits the standard baseline instrument.

The text says 28 speaking stops but the printed departments total 29 (Great 11, Swell 11, Pedal 7); all 29 printed stops are included. The pedal compass is not stated, so the default 32-note range is used.

ASSUMED MIDI channels: Great 1, Swell 2, Pedal 3. Phoenix lets the installer assign a channel to each department and publishes no defaults: check on the MIDI monitor and correct the channels before recording.

Stop changes are sent and received over MIDI, but the message format is not published (Hauptwerk's console presets describe Phoenix stops as Program Change on/off messages split across adjacent channels, with no per-model number table), so every stop is unbound: use Learn every stop.
The expression pedals send MIDI data, but the controller numbers are not published, so no expression is set: learn them from the MIDI monitor if needed.

Phoenix baseline organs let the customer choose the sample for each stop position, so stop names on your console may differ; the layout (stops per department, couplers) is fixed. Two built-in specifications can be selected on the LCD display.
Stop list: https://www.phoenixorgans.co.uk/pdfs/baseline.pdf (Phoenix Organs 'Baseline Organs' PDF, Feb 2005; also https://www.phoenixorgans.co.uk/sample2man.html and sample3man.html)

MIDI scheme: https://www.phoenixorgans.co.uk/pdfs/baseline.pdf (External Connections: "Midi IN, Post Coupled OUT, Pre Coupled OUT (Data from/for expression pedals, stop changes sent and received via midi)")

MIDI scheme: https://www.phoenixorgans.co.uk/pdfs/phoenix-system.pdf (System Capabilities table: MIDI "Assignable Channel for each dept." for In, Out 1 (pre-coupled) and Out 2 (post-coupled); no default channel numbers or message formats given)
